detail.title: Robustness and Redundancy in Quantum and Classical Records
detail.summary: Robustness in physical records is achieved when system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom, enabling consistent retrieval by independent observers through Spectrum Broadcast Structures. This mechanism persists across classical and quantum regimes, though it is modified by the specific noise-tolerance threshold of the observer's aperture function.
